finding.title: Wire core/learning/completion_constants.dart's kBulkPriorSentinelMs into its would-be callers instead of leaving it dead and re-duplicated 3x
finding.rule: Fowler-duplication / Evans (invariant re-derived instead of enforced in one place)

evidence.quote: These constants are used across domain services and providers to identify
core→features layering violation and is the single source of truth for the

finding.why: completion_constants.dart's docstring claims kBulkPriorSentinelMs is 'used across domain services and providers,' but a repo-wide grep shows zero imports of this file anywhere in lib/ or test/ — it is dead code. Meanwhile SchedulerEngine, BulkPriorCompletionService, and StreakRestorer each independently hand-redefine the identical magic literal 946684800000 (DateTime.utc(2000,1,1)). Two of the three duplicate definitions explicitly self-describe as 'the single source of truth,' a direct contradiction between files. All copies currently agree, so there is no live bug today, but the sentinel governs whether a completion counts toward streak/daily-bar-chart 'live activity' — if any one of the 4 independent copies is ever edited (e.g. during the W3.27-style migrations already underway elsewhere in this codebase) without updating the others, gamification data would silently miscategorize bulk-imported completions as live activity or vice versa for affected users, with no compiler or test signal since nothing imports the canonical constant to compare against.
finding.recommendation: Pick one true source (core/learning/completion_constants.dart is the natural core-layer home) and have SchedulerEngine, BulkPriorCompletionService, and StreakRestorer import and reuse it; if a core→features layering constraint genuinely blocks that, document why in coding-standards.md and delete the now-provably-false 'used across... providers' claim from whichever copy remains a local duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: grep for the literal 946684800000 (or DateTime.utc(2000, 1, 1) used as a sentinel) outside test/ resolves to exactly one definition plus its importers, not 4 independent literals.
core/learning/completion_constants.dart's docstring claim is verifiably true (has real importers) or the file is removed.

Existing bulk-prior/streak/scheduler regression tests continue passing after de-duplication (points_service_test.dart, chart_data_service tests, streak tests already reference the sentinel and act as the regression check).

finding.title: Wire up or delete the 4 unused core/domain/value_objects/ types (Pin, StageOrder, ScopeLevel/ScopeValue/CurriculumScope, CalendarSystem)

evidence.quote: class CurriculumScope extends DataClass implements Insertable<CurriculumScope> {

finding.why: A repo-wide grep for constructor/import usage of Pin, StageOrder, ScopeLevel, ScopeValue, CurriculumScope (the domain VO), and CalendarSystem finds zero call sites in lib/ outside their own files — each is exercised only by its own unit test. This isn't a harmless unused-import: it has a concrete duplication cost (set_parent_pin_use_case.dart independently hand-rolls the exact same `^\d{4}$` regex Pin.parse already implements, so the 4-digit PIN invariant now has two unlinked sources of truth) and a naming-collision cost (the domain `CurriculumScope` in scope.dart and the Drift-generated row class `CurriculumScope` in user_database.g.dart are two unrelated types with the identical name, which is exactly what would happen if the intended repository→domain mapping was never implemented). Each of these 4 files also drags a full unit-test file along for code that provides zero runtime value today, inflating the maintenance surface with no compensating benefit.
finding.recommendation: For each: either finish the primitive-obsession migration the docstrings reference (route set_parent_pin_use_case.dart through Pin, route curriculum_scope_dao.dart mapping through ScopeLevel/ScopeValue/CurriculumScope, adopt StageOrder/CalendarSystem at their intended call sites) or delete the type and its test if there is no near-term plan to adopt it.
acceptance_criteria: For each of Pin/StageOrder/ScopeLevel-ScopeValue-CurriculumScope/CalendarSystem: at least one production (non-test) import exists, or the file + its test are removed.
set_parent_pin_use_case.dart's hand-rolled `_isNumeric` regex is replaced by (or asserted equivalent to) Pin.parse's validation once a decision is made.
No two public top-level classes in lib/ share the name CurriculumScope (AG-4).

finding.title: Give StartDateWindowException a stable error code instead of a raw pre-formatted English message (EH-5)

evidence.quote: 'Program start date cannot be in the future. '

finding.why: EH-5 requires domain/data errors to carry stable codes/enums rather than pre-formatted human messages, specifically because this is an EN+Hebrew app where a raw English string renders untranslated for Hebrew-locale users. StartDateWindowException (thrown from the live B2/B3 date-window invariant, reached via ProgramStartingPosition.fromLegacyGrammar → track_blueprint.dart) is constructed with a fully-formatted English sentence, and it extends AppException whose only payload field is `final String message` — there is no code/enum to key an ARB lookup off. A repo-wide grep found no catch site for StartDateWindowException anywhere in lib/, so if the 30-day window is ever violated by legacy/migrated data (not just live UI input, which the picker constrains), the raw English text is the only representation available to whatever eventually surfaces it to the user.
finding.recommendation: Add a stable code/enum to StartDateWindowException (or to the AppException hierarchy generally) and have the presentation layer resolve it via AppLocalizations instead of displaying `message` directly.
acceptance_criteria: StartDateWindowException exposes a stable, locale-independent identifier (enum/const code) alongside or instead of the free-text message.
Any UI that surfaces this exception resolves the user-facing string via AppLocalizations/ARB, verified by an EN+HE widget test.

finding.title: Replace hardcoded 'cloudBorn' literal and profile_model.dart's reimplemented switch with AccountTier/ProfileMode's own storageKey/fromStorageKey
finding.rule: Fowler-duplication (self-flagged by each VO's own 'Migration note')

evidence.quote: Direct string comparisons (`profile.mode == 'child'`) should be replaced

finding.why: account_tier.dart's own docstring names exactly this anti-pattern as the W5.11 sweep target, yet the primary caller of DeviceRegistryDatabase.updateAccountTier (the local→cloud upgrade flow) hardcodes the raw literal 'cloudBorn' at all 4 of its call sites instead of using AccountTier.cloud.storageKey — the read path (DeviceAccountX.accountTier) already goes through the typed enum, so write and read now use two unlinked representations of the same key. Separately, profile_model.dart re-implements ProfileMode's string↔enum mapping with its own switch (silently defaulting to adult) instead of calling ProfileMode.fromStorageKey (which throws on unrecognized values). Neither currently misbehaves — the literals happen to match — but a typo or a future storage-key rename in the VO would not be caught by the compiler at any of these 5 sites, and the two ProfileMode mappings already have different error-handling semantics (throw vs. silent default) for what is meant to be the same conversion.
finding.recommendation: Replace the 4 'cloudBorn' literals with AccountTier.cloud.storageKey; have profile_model.dart's profileMode getter delegate to ProfileMode.fromStorageKey (wrapped in the same kind of fail-safe try/catch pattern already used in child_mode_guard.dart) instead of re-switching.
acceptance_criteria: upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart contains zero raw 'cloudBorn'/'localBorn' string literals; all go through AccountTier.*.storageKey.
profile_model.dart's profileMode getter calls ProfileMode.fromStorageKey (or documents why it deliberately diverges).

finding.title: Migrate core/domain/value_objects/ hand-written ==/hashCode/toString classes to @freezed
finding.rule: Naming/placement — "Domain/state models are immutable @freezed classes; never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes"
finding.why: Every non-enum class in this batch (Pin; ProgramStartingPosition; DelaySchedule/WeeklySchedule/RollingSchedule; ScopeLevel/ScopeValue/CurriculumScope; SefariaRef; StageOrder; StudyDayPattern — 10 classes across 7 files) hand-writes operator==/hashCode/toString rather than using @freezed, contrary to the stated codebase convention. All the ones I traced are currently correct, so this is not a live bug, but it is the exact pattern the standard calls out as risky: every future field addition to any of these classes requires manually keeping three methods in sync by hand with no compiler help, whereas @freezed generates all three from the field list and can't drift.
finding.recommendation: Migrate these VOs to @freezed where the validating-factory pattern (private const constructor + public validating factory) fits, which all of these already structurally resemble; note any VO where freezed genuinely doesn't fit as a documented exception in coding-standards.md rather than leaving it a silent inconsistency.
acceptance_criteria: New or materially-changed value objects in core/domain/value_objects/ use @freezed, or coding-standards.md documents an explicit lightweight-VO exception.
No behavior change: existing equality/hashCode/toString tests for these 7 files continue passing unmodified after any migration.
